newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UBS to take 3.0 bln Sfr charge.
newsitem.headline: UBS to take 3.0 bln Sfr charge.

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland said it will take a one-time charge of 3.0 billion Swiss francs to resolve loan problems, that will result in a group loss for 1996.
In announcing a restructuring of its domestic operations, UBS also said that after reviewing the planned measures, Standard & Poor's has put it on its credit watch list.
But rating agencies Moody's and IBCA have confirmed the bank's long-term AAA rating.
UBS chief executive Mathis Cabiallavetta said that prior to a 1.4 billion credit risk charge, 1996 group profit would have been around 1.8 billion Swiss francs.
This figure will now be reduced by 3.0 billion Swiss francs for the special credit risk provision, and a provision of 120 million for restructuring costs in Switzerland.

He said the resulting negative balance for the group of about 1.3 billion francs will be narrowed to what it estimates to be in the region of about "half a billion" francs by the release of 711 million francs in reserves for general banking risks (which rank as equity capital) and a reduction in tax expense on account of weaker earnings.
"This is roughly the loss which the Group will report at the end of the year," Cabiallavetta said in a speech prepared for a news conference.
He also said that, after these measures have been implemented, group equity will amount to 21.5 billion francs at the end of this yera, compared with 23 billion at the end of 1995.
